#### 1. Zimmermann-Laband syndrome 1  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.791)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:6250)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNH1 (HGNC:6250) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); KCNH1 (HGNC:6250) —LEADS_TO→ Global developmental delay (HP:0001263); KCNH1 (HGNC:6250) —LEADS_TO→ Epilepsy (HP:0001250); KCNH1 (HGNC:6250) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal facial skeletal morphology (HP:0000241); KCNH1 (HGNC:6250) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal corpus callosum morphology (HP:0033730). Haploinsufficiency of KCNH1 leads to a spectrum of neurological and craniofacial phenotypes common to both MONDO:0012735 and Zimmermann-Laband syndrome 1.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in KCNH1 with consistent loss-of-function effects in patients diagnosed with MONDO:0012735 and Zimmermann-Laband syndrome 1 would support this hypothesis. Conversely, identification of distinct causal genes or divergent functional consequences of KCNH1 variants in the two diseases would falsify it. _(variant: The presence of common benign variants in KCNH1 in the gnomAD database that are implicated in both conditions.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic etiology of MONDO:0012735 and Zimmermann-Laband syndrome 1 through KCNH1 haploinsufficiency could facilitate the development of targeted therapeutic strategies for overlapping clinical features, potentially improving diagnostic yield and patient outcomes.

#### 2. intellectual disability, autosomal dominant 46  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.434)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-1296072)

**Proposed mechanism:** KCNH1 (HGNC:6266) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal excitability (GO:0007228); KCNQ5 (HGNC:19071) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal excitability (GO:0007228); neuronal excitability (GO:0007228) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); neuronal excitability (GO:0007228) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in KCNH1 or KCNQ5 with significantly different functional consequences (e.g., one being a strong loss-of-function and the other a strong gain-of-function) that cannot be reconciled with the proposed haploinsufficiency model for both diseases. _(variant: gnomad v2.1.1 or v3.1.2 allele frequency > 0.01 for any pathogenic variant in KCNH1 or KCNQ5)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of KCNH1 and KCNQ5 in neuronal excitability could lead to identifying common therapeutic targets for both rare diseases, potentially involving modulation of ion channel activity.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that mutations in KCNH1 and KCNC1 affect entirely distinct cellular pathways that do not converge on neuronal excitability, or identification of distinct functional consequences (e.g., one requires gain-of-function and the other loss-of-function) for both genes. _(variant: Discovery of common variants (e.g., allele frequency > 1% in gnomAD) in KCNH1 or KCNC1 that are strongly associated with either disease.)_
